svg.title: Layered Logic Mirror — Pattern Designer screen wireframe (post-V1 mockup)
svg.desc: Speculative V2/post-V1 mockup of a pattern designer screen for the Layered Logic Mirror app. Not built in V1 — V1 ships 7 fixed patterns from firmware (solid, rainbow, scanner, spinner, random, breathing, twinkle). This mockup explores the natural extension: a guided editor where users pick a base pattern algorithm, tune its parameters (speed, hue range, brightness modulation), and save with a name. Shows a live 6x6 LED preview at top, base-pattern chip selector, parameter sliders, and save controls. 6 numbered callouts pairing each design hypothesis to the question it raises. 4 alternate-state thumbnails: solid color, library view, save dialog, blank-canvas "Custom" mode. Visually marked as POST-V1 throughout. Phone proportions match Pixel 9 (360x800 dp).
svg.text: Speculative · Layered Logic Mirror · App/v2 (not built) · Mobile
Live preview — updates as you tune parameters
Saves to your library — share/export coming soon.
Live preview is the central UX
Without seeing what you're making, the editor is abstract
parameter knobs. Place preview at top so it stays visible while
scrolling through params. Updates in real-time as you tune —
requires firmware-side preview op (cheap WS message, no commit).
Hypothesis · firmware preview op spec TBD
Start from a base, don't start blank
Guided editing: 8 base pattern algorithms (the 7 V1 ship-with
plus "Custom" for the more abstract V3 path). Each base has its
own parameter set. Blank-canvas creation is intimidating and the
time investment isn't worth it for most users (per Govee/Nanoleaf
precedent — both ship preset-tuning, not blank-canvas).
Parameters specific to each base pattern
Rainbow: Speed + Hue range + Brightness mod. Scanner: Speed +
Tail + Bounce/Wrap. Solid: just color. Each base exposes the
parameters that actually matter for that algorithm — not a
universal "everything" panel. Picking a different base swaps the
Open question: do users want to discover params, or is it overwhelming?
"1.2 s/cycle" beats "Speed: 65". Real units give the user a
concrete model of what's about to happen. Cost: each slider
needs unit-aware min/max + step. Pays back in fewer
Hypothesis · check against power-user vs casual segmentation
Reuse V1 color wheel for color params
When the base is Solid (or any pattern with a single-color param),
tap into the parameter row and the existing color wheel from
Home/Controls slides up. Consistency over parallel implementations —
the wheel already has scroll-lock, magnifier, hex display.
Save with a name → goes into the user's library → shows up in
Home/Controls pattern grid alongside the V1 presets. Library
community gallery — far-future) presume named, addressable units.
Different base patterns swap the param set. Saved-patterns library, save dialog, and the speculative "Custom" blank-canvas path.
Solid has one param: color. The whole
params section collapses to a single
field; tapping it opens the V1 color
Library lives in Settings or as a tab on
Pattern Designer. Tap a row to edit;
Modal over the designer; default name
mirror has a name set. Saving routes
user back to Home/Controls with the
tuning. Out of scope until V2 ships.
Blank-canvas path is a real V3+ thing
but speculative even relative to V2.
Showing it here so the design rationale
captures the full vision, not just V2.
